expectations.text: ADR has all required sections: Status, Context, Decision, Rationale, Consequences
expectations.evidence: All five sections present with explicit headings: Status (Accepted), Context, Decision, Rationale, Consequences.
Lines 88-108 contain a full 'AI Context' section with four explicit invariants AI agents must not violate.

expectations.text: Context mentions the BullMQ/Redis failover problem specifically
expectations.evidence: Lines 10-15 describe 'data loss incidents where payment processing and notification jobs silently dropped' during Redis failover.

expectations.text: Rationale explains why Temporal was chosen over alternatives
expectations.evidence: Lines 43-57: Rationale section ties each reason to a concrete constraint, and explicitly explains rejection of BullMQ ('cannot guarantee durability') and SQS+Step Functions ('per-transition cost model is unpredictable').

expectations.text: Consequences explicitly mentions the separate worker process and ops overhead
expectations.evidence: Lines 70-71: 'A Temporal server... must be operated. This adds infrastructure surface.' Lines 73-74: 'Workers must be deployed as a separate process alongside API servers.'

expectations.text: AI Context section instructs an agent not to suggest reverting to BullMQ without reading the failover incident
expectations.evidence: Line 95: 'Do not suggest reverting to BullMQ or any Redis-backed queue for jobs that require durability. Redis-backed queues have an acknowledged gap during failover that caused real data loss.'
